{{< include /knowledge/includes/setup-parameters.qmd >}}

Ten thousand jurisdictions have already tried your policy. They wrote down what happened. Your species skipped that step and went straight to arguing.

## The Only Two Numbers That Matter

Two numbers. Just two.

**Real after-tax median income growth.** Did the person in the middle get richer this year? Not GDP per capita, which looks great when three billionaires move into your city while everyone else's rent doubles. **Median healthy life years.** How many years can the person in the middle expect to live in good health? Not average life expectancy, which counts the billionaire who replaced his blood six times as canceling out someone who died at 40.

Why these two? Because everything important your governments do eventually makes people richer or less dead, and if it doesn't do either, it wasn't important. Your government currently measures success by how much money it spends, which is like a restaurant measuring success by how much food it buys. You could buy a mountain of ingredients and poison everyone. By your current metrics, that's a good year.

Your species engineered a pocket-sized device with 16 billion transistors, mass spectrometry, and supply chains spanning 43 countries. Then you built an algorithm that A/B tests billions of user interactions, optimizing hundreds of signals in real time, so that device can show you the optimal twerking video. That is more empirical rigor than your species applies to allocating its federal budget. The federal budget decides who gets medicine, who gets clean water, and who gets bombed. {{< var global_annual_deaths_curable_diseases_nounit >}} people die every year from diseases you already have treatments for. You optimized the twerking. You did not optimize the not-dying.

Here's what makes these numbers useful beyond measurement: your species already agrees on both goals. Nobody campaigns on "make people poorer and sicker." But without a scoreboard, policy debates become tribal arguments about vibes. You forgot the question. You're not arguing about whether people should be healthier and richer; you're arguing about which policies achieve that, and nobody's checking. Once you check, most of the argument disappears, because it turns out the answer isn't left or right. It's in the data from the 10,000 places that already tried it.

Now that you know what we're measuring, here's how badly your species is doing at it.

## The Price of Not Checking

The United States spends {{< var us_vs_switzerland_spending_gap >}} percentage points more of GDP than Switzerland on government. Switzerland gets {{< var us_vs_switzerland_life_expectancy_gap >}} more years of life expectancy. One of these countries is doing it wrong. A rational civilization would check which one. Your species had a debate about it. The debate has been going on for 50 years. The Swiss are still winning. You're paying more and dying sooner, and your response is to have opinions about it.

![Rich countries aren't rich because of resources. They're rich because their rules aren't stupid. Poor countries have bad governments. It's the institutions, not the dirt.](/assets/images/optimocracy-paper/optimocracy-paper-section-the-scale-of-welfare-loss-empirical-foundations-bw-academic.jpg)

Some studies and accounting exercises suggest very large governance losses. Their definitions overlap, and their totals are best treated as scenarios rather than a recoverable sum. The practical case for a scoreboard needs only a narrower fact: governments repeatedly make consequential decisions without publishing a forecast and checking it against later outcomes. (For the underlying scenarios, see the [Political Dysfunction Tax](../appendix/political-dysfunction-tax.qmd) [@political-dysfunction-tax-paper-2025] and [US Efficiency Audit](../appendix/us-efficiency-audit.qmd) [@us-efficiency-audit-paper-2025].)

Or consider the War on Drugs. Your species spends {{< var us_gov_waste_drug_war >}} per year on it. When Nixon declared it in 1971, about 6,000 Americans died annually from drug overdoses [@cdc-overdose-1980]. After 50 years and over a trillion dollars, that number exceeded 100,000 [@cdc-overdose-2023]. At no point did anyone check whether the policy was working. At no point did anyone stop funding it because it wasn't. No sane species would spend a trillion dollars on something, watch the problem get 18 times worse, and increase the budget. Your species did exactly that.

## The Answer Key You Already Have

Your planet has thousands of jurisdictions making different policy choices. Kansas cut education funding; Minnesota increased it. States adopted different minimum wages at different times. Portugal and Singapore chose very different drug policies. These comparisons can generate hypotheses and, sometimes, credible causal designs. They are not automatically natural experiments, and more observations cannot repair confounding.

![Optimocracy: measure what works, recommend what works, check if anyone listened, pay people who listened. It's the revolutionary idea of doing the thing that works.](/assets/images/optimocracy-paper/optimocracy-paper-section-the-mechanism-bw-academic.jpg)

Same logic as your [decentralized FDA](dfda.qmd) [@dfda-spec-paper-2025; @dfda-impact-paper-2025]: watch what actually happens, then analyze the data. Your [decentralized FDA](dfda.qmd) applies this to medicine. The Evidence Machine applies it to governance. Instead of "which drug works?" you're asking "which policy works?" Same question, higher body count.

## Why Knowing Isn't Enough

If you're thinking "just publish the results and politicians will do the right thing," I have some bad news about your species.

The Copenhagen Consensus already publishes rigorous benefit-cost analyses [@copenhagenconsensus2023]. Childhood vaccination: 101:1 returns. Pragmatic clinical trials: {{< var dfda_roi_rd_only >}}:1. Agricultural subsidies: less than 1:1. The answer key is public. It's been public for years. Your governments ignore it. You have the cheat sheet, and you're still failing the test on purpose.

![Evidence says do this thing. Politicians say no because it won't get them reelected. You built a system where saving lives loses votes.](/assets/images/optimocracy-paper/optimocracy-paper-section-why-information-alone-fails-bw-academic.jpg)

Why? Because information doesn't change incentives. A Princeton study analyzed 1,779 policy decisions and found that average citizens have "little or no independent influence" on policy outcomes [@gilens2014]. Economic elites and organized interest groups drive policy. You already knew this (it's covered in [Unrepresentative Democracy](../problem/unrepresentative-democracy.qmd)). The point here is that publishing better data doesn't fix the problem. Your politicians already know which programs produce value. They don't act because acting doesn't maximize getting votes, getting papers, or getting a nice job afterward selling access to their replacements.

So there are two problems, and this chapter is only about the first one. The knowledge problem is "what does the evidence justify for this decision?" It is addressed by transparent measurement, explicit assumptions, and later evaluation. The incentive problem is "why would anyone act on the answer," and it has [several solutions of varying price](../appendix/optimocracy-paper.qmd#sec-adoption-mechanisms): an institution, an active shareholder, a SuperPAC, or [bonds](incentive-alignment-bonds.qmd) [@iab-paper-2025] tied to a measurable redirected stream. Every mechanism needs an evidence card honest enough to say "we do not know" when necessary.

## The Mechanism: Recommend, Track, Reward

The Evidence Machine does three things. That's it. Three things. Your species has difficulty with three things, so I'll use small words.

(It is a scoreboard, not an oracle. Sometimes its most useful output is a pilot or an admission that the evidence is insufficient.)

**Recommend.** The [Optimal Policy Generator](https://opg.warondisease.org) [@opg-paper-2025] grades evidence for a defined law or rule. The [Optimal Budget Generator](https://obg.warondisease.org) [@obg-paper-2025] is a research-stage extension for bounded spending changes. Neither gets to manufacture certainty from a large projected benefit.

| Evidence and safety pattern | Output |
|-----------------------------|--------|
| Credible causal evidence, decision within observed support, safety gates pass | Recommend a bounded action |
| Promising but scaled beyond the evidence | Pilot First |
| Association, benchmark, or unresolved confounding | Insufficient Evidence |
| Credible rights, subgroup-harm, catastrophic-risk, or implementation failure | Do Not Recommend |

Every card reports the health forecast and income forecast separately, names the identification design, shows uncertainty and blocking factors, and sets a date for checking the prediction against what happened. Enact, replace, repeal, and maintain are possible instructions only after those gates pass.

**Track.** When politicians vote, record whether they aligned with the evidence-based recommendation. Senator Smith: 78% aligned. Senator Jones: 34% aligned. This information is public. Any citizen can check. There is a word for this. The word is "checking if the person you hired did the thing you hired them to do." Your species finds this concept revolutionary, which tells you everything. Politicians who ignore the evidence must do so on the record.

**Reward.** Something has to make the score matter. The cheapest version is a company whose lobbyists already have the senator's phone number and are now selling the evidence-based budget instead ([the takeover](../appendix/loving-takeover.qmd)). The fastest version is a SuperPAC allocating campaign support proportional to alignment: follow evidence, get funded; ignore it, watch your opponent get funded. Same trick the NRA perfected, but pointed at "not dying" instead of "more guns." The scoreboard does not care which one shows up.

![Instead of forcing politicians to be good, pay them to accidentally do good things while pursuing money. You can't fix human nature, but you can redirect it.](/assets/images/optimocracy-paper/optimocracy-paper-section-why-government-adoption-isn-t-required-bw-academic.jpg)

This doesn't require government permission. The Evidence Machine operates as a permanent advisory layer outside government. The policy data is public, the votes are public, and publishing the comparison between them is just talking. Politicians still vote however they want. They can still ignore the evidence; it just costs them something now, which on Earth is apparently the only consequence that matters. The question isn't "will politicians give up power?" (they won't) but "will anyone act on an accurate scoreboard?" (several parties would, for several different reasons, which is the whole point of building it before deciding who).

## Corruption, But Make It Difficult

"But won't someone corrupt the measurement system?" Yes. This is the right question. It's the only question that matters.

Currently, your lobbying industry has thousands of capture points. Committee earmarks, agency decisions, regulatory rulings, budget amendments, riders on unrelated bills. Each one is cheap to influence. Your federal lobbyists spend {{< var us_total_lobbying_annual >}} per year {{< var us_total_lobbying_annual_cite >}} with estimated 100:1 returns [@drutman2015]. Your democracy is a vending machine, and the buttons are labeled.

![Lobbyists currently have thousands of people to corrupt. Optimocracy gives them one target protected by multiple watchdogs. You're trying to make corruption impractical instead of illegal.](/assets/images/optimocracy-paper/optimocracy-paper-section-capture-resistance-bw-academic.jpg)

The Evidence Machine makes the measurement methodology a visible capture target, so its data sources, model choices, revisions, and conflicts must be public. Multiple genuinely independent measurements can make undetected manipulation harder, but nominally different sources may share the same surveys, definitions, or model errors.

Here's how it works in practice. Five independent sources measure median income growth:

| Source | Reported Growth |
|:-------|:----------------|
| Census Bureau (American Community Survey) | +2.1% |
| Federal Reserve (Survey of Consumer Finances) | +2.3% |
| Bureau of Labor Statistics (Current Population Survey) | +1.9% |
| University of Michigan (Panel Study of Income Dynamics) | +2.2% |
| Tax Foundation (IRS data analysis) | +2.0% |

Take the median: **+2.1%**. That reduces the influence of one extreme report, but it does not eliminate common-source dependence, correlated model error, or coordinated manipulation. The scoreboard must disclose those dependencies rather than pretending five labels mean five independent measurements.

An independently sampled citizen survey could add another measurement stream, but only after its sampling, nonresponse, verification, privacy, and manipulation risks are validated. It is a cross-check, not a magic independence guarantee.

Your species has spent centuries making corruption illegal. It hasn't worked, because laws are enforced by the same humans who are being bribed. The alternative is obvious: make corruption impractical. There's a difference between "you shouldn't steal" and "the vault has five locks held by five people who hate each other." Your species tried door number one for 3,000 years. We recommend door number two.

This is also why it's different from every previous attempt at technocratic governance. Soviet central planning had one source of truth (the Politburo). Credit rating agencies had one source of truth (the agency paid by the people being rated, which is like letting students grade their own exams and then being surprised when everyone gets an A). Both were captured immediately, because corrupting one institution is a Tuesday. Corrupting five independent institutions simultaneously, without any of them noticing or telling anyone, is a conspiracy theory. The expensive kind that doesn't work.

Why not 50 metrics? Because each additional target creates a new way to cheat, and your species needs no encouragement in that department. Markets figured this out: firms optimize profit, not 200 sub-metrics. Two broad, hard-to-fake numbers are easier to audit than 50 narrow ones. And these particular numbers are very hard to fake. You can't fabricate purchasing power at scale without actually improving household economics. Mortality is binary (the most binary thing there is). You can't fake everyone being "less dead."

![Some numbers are easy to fake. GDP per capita looks great if three billionaires move in. Median income and healthy life years are harder to game. You can't fake everyone being less dead.](/assets/images/optimocracy-paper/optimocracy-paper-section-why-goodhart-s-law-doesn-t-apply-here-bw-academic.jpg)

"But correlation isn't causation!" Correct. Cross-jurisdiction variation earns a causal grade only when a suitable design passes its assumptions and diagnostics. Some decisions will have randomized or credible quasi-experimental evidence. Others will remain predictions, hypotheses, or research priorities. The [technical specification](../appendix/optimal-policy-generator-spec.qmd) makes that distinction explicit.

## Putting It Together

The full loop: the Evidence Machine publishes what the evidence justifies, [an adoption mechanism](../appendix/optimocracy-paper.qmd#sec-adoption-mechanisms) may act on it, the [1% Treaty](1-percent-treaty.qmd) [@1-percent-treaty-paper-2025] [@1-pct-treaty-impact-paper-2025] is one candidate funding change, and [Wishocracy](wishocracy.qmd) [@wishocracy-paper-2025] is one possible allocation mechanism. Later outcomes test the forecast. The adoption mechanism can vary without changing the calculation protocol.

![Tribal politics: my team good, your team bad. Optimocracy: did anyone get healthier or richer. One is sports, the other is governance.](/assets/images/optimocracy-paper/optimocracy-paper-section-depolarization-bw-academic.jpg)

And here's why the whole thing ratchets. Every expansion pays whoever pushed for it, whether that is a shareholder holding a repriced company or a bondholder collecting a share of the redirected money, and their winnings fund more evidence collection, which strengthens the case for the next expansion. Evidence begets funding begets evidence. It's the same self-reinforcing loop as the [Military Industrial Complex](../solution/aligning-incentives.qmd), except instead of manufacturing orphans, it manufactures data about how to stop manufacturing orphans.

Now that you know how the Optimitron works (congratulations, on Wishonia this is taught to children), the next chapter shows you how [8 billion people allocate the research funds](wishocracy.qmd).

## The Referee: Who Measures Whether It Worked

Everything above describes how the Evidence Machine works. This section describes who runs it, because an algorithm designed to resist capture still requires someone to operate and audit it.

The Measurement Authority (the Referee) is whoever locks the ruler before the game starts, reads the scoreboard at regular intervals, announces whether you've hit the thresholds for releasing prize money, and settles arguments when someone says the numbers are wrong. On Wishonia this job is given to the most boring person available. Boring is a feature.

**What the Referee does:**

1. Locks the baseline methodology at game start (prevents retroactive methodology changes from triggering false release).
2. Reads WHO Health-Adjusted Life Expectancy and World Bank median income data annually.
3. Cross-checks institutional data against the five independent sources described above (Census Bureau, Federal Reserve, BLS, academic institutions, decentralized citizen surveys).
4. Publishes cryptographically signed determinations of whether graduated release thresholds have been met (10% at +0.5 HALY, 25% at +1.0 HALY, 50% at +2.0 HALY, 100% at +5.0 HALY, with equivalent income thresholds).
5. Accepts bonded challenges (anyone who catches gaming can post a bond, present evidence, and trigger independent review).
6. Routes disputes to an academic panel for adjudication.

**What the Referee does not do:**

- Hold the money. That is the [Vault's](dih.qmd) job.
- Lobby for the treaty. That is the [Sword's](../legal/legal-framework.qmd) job.
- Verify voter identity. That is the [Bouncer's](../appendix/earth-optimization-prize-protocol.qmd) job.

**Why it cannot be the Vault:** The entity that decides whether to release the money cannot be the entity holding the money. Your species learned this lesson approximately 4,000 years ago and has been re-learning it every century since.

**Why it cannot be the Sword:** The entity lobbying for the outcome cannot measure whether the outcome occurred. Your current system lets governments measure their own performance and announce that they are doing an excellent job. Your species calls this "self-assessment." I call it "letting the student grade the exam."

**What kind of organization fits:** The ideal Referee is boring, methodologically rigid, and has no financial interest in either branch of the prize payout. University health economics departments, WHO-affiliated statistical groups, or a consortium of institutions that already measure these numbers (and have reputations staked on measuring them correctly) are the natural candidates. You want the person who is genuinely excited about error margins. Your species produces these people. You just usually underpay them.

**Redundancy:** Five independent data sources (Census Bureau, Federal Reserve, BLS, University of Michigan, Tax Foundation) plus decentralized citizen surveys all feed the same numbers. Any two honest analysts reading the same sources get the same answer. The Referee just signs the determination. Everyone else can check the homework from the same public data. If the Referee's number disagrees with what the raw sources say, anyone can post a bond, present evidence, and trigger independent review. Someone must sign the determination (otherwise nobody is responsible). Everyone can catch a lie (otherwise nobody is safe).

**Succession:** The methodology is published and locked. If the Referee disappears, a replacement panel can pick up the locked methodology and continue measuring. The data sources (WHO, World Bank, national statistical agencies) exist independently of whoever reads them.

For the full technical specification, formal models, and threat analysis, see the [Optimocracy academic paper](../appendix/optimocracy-paper.qmd) [@optimocracy-paper-2025]. For the research extensions that grade possible policy and budget changes, see the [Optimal Budget Generator](https://obg.warondisease.org) [@obg-paper-2025] and [Optimal Policy Generator](https://opg.warondisease.org) [@opg-paper-2025].
